is a leading behavioral health organization that supported over 48,000 youth and adults across six counties in Northern California and the San Francisco Bay Area last year.

Caminar's mission
is to build strength and stability through comprehensive mental health and substance use treatment and wrap-around services delivered through evidence-based, whole-person care. The organization was founded in 1964, and our vision

jobs.description:
The rewards at Healogics are immense, starting with the important work we do to change patients’ lives. We also understand that meaningful work is hard work, and we are committed to supporting and compensating our employees for the tremendous service they provide.

Think you are a great fit? Learn more about this role here:

Healogics is the largest provider of advanced wound care services in the United States, treating more than 300,000 chronic wound patients annually across over 600 sites. With an aging society, obesity and diabetes on the rise, and an uptick in surgical procedures, the number of patients with non-healing wounds that would benefit from expert care is dramatically increasing. As a result, the company is working to provide our differentiated, quality outcomes to as many patients that would benefit through our out-patient clinic partnerships

The Program Director or Program Manager is responsible for the management and the strategic growth of the Wound Care Program for the assigned area of responsibility. This position is responsible for the complete oversight of the Wound Care Center, to include the following functions: day-to-day center operations, staff management, financial management, quality/performance improvement, and community education. The Program Director/Program Manager is also responsible for maintaining collaborative and consultative client relationships within and outside the hospital organization and for creating effective working relationships between Healogics and the hospital.

All Healogics employees must perform their job responsibilities according to all Healogics policies, Hospital policies, as well as to accrediting organizations, federal and state regulation, and to the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) guidelines, as applicable.

Essential Functions/Responsibilities: (Percentage times shown in parenthesis next to each function)

Manages the Center’s Operations (20%):

Oversees the day-to-day management of outpatient clinic(s) and other wound continuum programs, as applicable.
Continuously assesses current clinic flows, processes and procedures, identifies areas of improvement, and develops and implements best practices and appropriate changes to improve outcomes, using the company’s resources.
Works with hospital and company personnel to ensure availability of adequate resources, supplies, equipment and services.
Facilitates the flow of information and maximizes effective communication throughout the program.
Prioritizes responsibilities and directs the work of the Center’s clinical staff and non- clinical staff.
Collaborates with other health care providers, Wound Care Center Providers, and Medical Director regarding clinic and patient needs.
Manages direct reports in conjunction with the company and hospital HR departments. This includes interviewing, hiring, motivating, coaching, counselling, establishing performance expectations, and conducting performance reviews. (5%)

Performs Financial Management (10%)

Manages and coordinates all aspects of the revenue cycle for Healogics and for the hospital partner, as appropriate.
Stays current with reimbursement changes, providing physician and staff updates and education as needed.
Reviews key financial reports, identifies key indicator trends and develops plans to implement best practices to ensure fiscal responsibility.
Tracks and reports all ancillary revenues generated by the program.
Manages costs through appropriate utilization and management of labor and supply.
Works with Healogics support team to complete financial reviews and presents results to hospital leadership.

Manages Community Education/Marketing functions (40%)

Works directly with the hospital and Healogics marketing departments to ensure that the wound care program has established strategic marketing plans and works with the same group and the hospital physician liaison to plan, coordinate, and execute activities directed toward increasing patient referrals to the wound care center(s).
Works collaboratively, as part of a multi-functional team, to best determine key target referral sources, and develops a systematic approach to build those customer relationships and increase wound care center referrals.
Maintains, monitors and updates the list of Physician Practice(s) within a given radius of the hospital on an ongoing basis.
Visits Physician Practices and interacts with key physicians to provide awareness of the Wound Care Center program, using educational marketing materials. Also documents all physician office interactions, as well as the visits with the Physician Practices in the Healogics Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system.

Participates in hospital committees as appropriate and ensures timely and accurate documentation in the patient record and outcomes database.
Monitors patient, referring physician and customer satisfaction.
Ensures that Patient Safety Guidelines are followed, that Healogics employees complete annual compliance requirements, and creates an environment that promotes the escalation of compliance concerns as appropriate.

Manages Relationships (15%)

Maintains excellent relationship with hospital client and continuously seeks to understand needs, confirm goal alignment and demonstrate value proposition. Identifies the hospital strategic goals and objectives and manages the program to achieve those goals, while remaining compliant with all Healogics operations standards. Works effectively and seamlessly at all levels within the partner hospital. Participates in hospital department/management meetings and actively participates in Hospital communication activities.
Builds and develops effective working relationships with panel physicians, clinical and support staff. Encourages all program staff to provide excellent customer service to members of other hospital departments.
Meets regularly with leadership including hospital and area management.
Performs other duties as required.

OR Associate’s degree in Business Administration, Healthcare Administration, Nursing or related field preferred and 2 or more years of marketing/community education in the healthcare industry or clinical operations experience

The Program Director is a key leader responsible for supporting the growth of Keck Medicine of USC through the strategic oversight of mergers, acquisitions, and community physician alignment initiatives. This role owns the end-to-end due diligence and integration lifecycle for assigned transactions, ensuring initiatives align with organizational strategy and long-term system goals. The Program Director partners closely with executive leadership, physicians, and cross-functional teams to evaluate opportunities throughout the deal continuum, design scalable operating models, and deliver successful integrations. This role requires strong business judgment, payer and value-based care acumen, and the ability to design community physician alignment models aligned with future-state needs, ensuring initiatives drive sustainable, long-term value for the health system.

Lead and own due diligence, integration planning, and implementation for community physician alignment, M&A, and partnership initiatives that support health system growth.

Provide analytical leadership in support of the Transformation Office, including assessing operational, financial, and synergy impacts of diligence findings and integration plans.

Drive continuous improvement by standardizing best practices, identifying efficiencies, and enhancing the physician and partner experience across transactions, while supporting the ongoing development of the Transformation Office’s deal management system.

jobs.title: Chief Development Officer
jobs.description:
The University of Southern California seeks an accomplished advancement leader to serve as Chief Development Officer (CDO) for the USC Suzanne Dworak-Peck School of Social Work.

Reporting to the Dean of the USC Suzanne Dworak-Peck School of Social Work, with a dotted-line relationship to the Vice President, Health Sciences Advancement, the CDO serves as the School’s senior fundraising executive and leads all aspects of its comprehensive development program. The CDO is responsible for planning, organizing, developing, implementing, and executing short- and long-term strategies to secure major, principal, and transformational gifts from individuals, alumni, foundations, corporations, and other philanthropic partners.

Working closely with the Dean, Board of Councilors members, faculty, staff, volunteers, Health Sciences Advancement colleagues and university leadership, the CDO advances the school’s strategic priorities through philanthropy. The position oversees fundraising strategy, donor engagement, stewardship, volunteer management, development operations, and staff leadership while serving as a key ambassador for the USC Suzanne Dworak-Peck School and USC.

The successful candidate will maintain an active portfolio of leadership and principal gift prospects and will be expected to personally secure significant philanthropic investments that advance the school’s highest priorities. The CDO will also recruit, develop, mentor, and retain a high-performing advancement team while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, and donor-centered engagement.

The CDO will be expected to build a pipeline of seven- and eight-figure philanthropic opportunities and play a leading role in positioning the school for future university-wide campaign initiatives and transformational fundraising efforts.

Opportunity

The USC Suzanne Dworak-Peck School of Social Work offers an exceptional opportunity to advance one of the nation's leading schools of social work and a recognized leader in improving health and social outcomes for individuals, families, and communities.

Nationally recognized for excellence in behavioral health, military social work, telehealth innovation, workforce development, health equity, aging, child welfare, juvenile justice, homelessness, responsible artificial intelligence, and community-based solutions, the school addresses society's most pressing challenges through pioneering research, innovative education, and meaningful community partnerships.

Working collaboratively with distinguished faculty, researchers, practitioners, university leadership, the School's Board of Councilors, Central Advancement, and Health Sciences Advancement colleagues, the Chief Development Officer (CDO) will lead comprehensive fundraising efforts that advance the school's strategic priorities. Through the cultivation and stewardship of philanthropic partnerships, the CDO will secure philanthropic investments that support groundbreaking research, innovative academic programs, scholarships and student stipend programs, faculty excellence, and community engagement initiatives that expand opportunity and improve health and well-being.

Ideal Candidate Profile

The USC Suzanne Dworak-Peck School seeks a strategic and mission-driven development leader who combines exceptional fundraising expertise with a deep appreciation for the ways social work drives meaningful health and social impact.

The successful candidate will bring demonstrated success securing major and principal gifts, leading comprehensive fundraising programs, managing high-performing teams, and cultivating relationships with sophisticated donors and stakeholders. We welcome candidates with advancement leadership experience across higher education, academic health systems, health affairs, community health organizations, foundations, social impact organizations, public service institutions, and other mission-driven sectors.

The strongest candidates understand that they are fundraising around human outcomes, systems change, health equity, behavioral health, workforce development, community impact, and social determinants of health. They can position social work not simply as an academic discipline, but as an essential driver of healthier individuals, stronger communities, and improved outcomes across populations.

The ideal candidate is a development leader who understands how social work improves health outcomes, advances behavioral health, strengthens communities, addresses structural barriers to well-being, and supports the broader health ecosystem. They possess the ability to translate these impacts into compelling philanthropic opportunities that resonate with foundations, community leaders, advocates, alumni, grateful patients, and other donors committed to social change and community impact.

Key Responsibilities Will Include The Following

Lead the planning, implementation, and execution of comprehensive fundraising and stewardship strategies in support of the USC Suzanne Dworak-Peck School’s mission and strategic priorities.
Secure major, principal, and transformational gifts from individuals, alumni, foundations, corporations, and other philanthropic partners.
Partner with the Dean, faculty, and university leadership to identify funding priorities and develop philanthropic opportunities aligned with institutional goals.
Identify, cultivate, solicit, and steward prospective and current donors while expanding and strengthening the School’s donor pipeline.
Represent the USC Suzanne Dworak-Peck School to donors, alumni, foundations, corporations, community leaders, volunteers, advocates, and other key stakeholders.
Translate complex research, community-based initiatives, workforce development programs, and policy-focused efforts into compelling cases for philanthropic investment.
Build relationships with philanthropic partners interested in behavioral health, health equity, community impact, workforce development, vulnerable populations, and systems-level change.
Plan and direct donor visits, engagement opportunities, and special events that advance fundraising objectives.
Collaborate with university partners to develop donor communications, fundraising materials, impact stories, and stewardship initiatives.
Encourage and support faculty engagement with foundations, community partners, and corporate organizations and facilitate philanthropic proposals when appropriate.
Develop and oversee the annual development budget and ensure effective stewardship of resources.
Recruit, mentor, and lead development staff, fostering a collaborative, high-performing, and inclusive team culture.
Establish goals, monitor progress, provide coaching and feedback, and empower staff and volunteers through active communication and leadership.
Maintain awareness of legal, regulatory, and policy developments affecting philanthropy and higher education advancement.
Promote a workplace culture where all employees are valued, value others, and have the opportunity to contribute through their ideas, words, and actions in accordance with the USC Code of Ethics.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree
Eight (8) years of professional experience within university advancement/development setting
Experience in planning development efforts in support of institutional and departmental strategies, and managing and leading goal-oriented teams
Experience in academic and/or higher education development, collaborating with prominent faculty, and working understanding of university research units
Demonstrated track record of success securing major gifts and meeting fundraising goals

jobs.description:
About the Company

Qrkiez is a technology platform transforming how families, individuals, and professionals connect within the neurodivergent care space. Its mission is to empower authentic connections between the neurodivergent community and the professionals who champion their success. Roughly one in five children in the United States is neurodivergent, yet a large share of those individuals and their families struggle to find the right care, and many parents of neurodivergent children report feeling isolated and alone. Qrkiez was built to close that gap.

The platform brings together three pillars that the market has historically kept fragmented: a curated directory of vetted service providers across education, coaching, life skills, enrichment, and wellness; online communities where families and neurodivergent individuals share stories and find belonging; and a wealth of trusted resources and content that cut through the noise and misinformation surrounding neurodivergence. Families and individuals, called QuirkyExplorers, join and use Qrkiez for free, while service providers, called QuirkyPros, build detailed profiles, join or start communities, and engage at no upfront cost.

The transformation Qrkiez brings to the industry is its AI-powered matching engine. Rather than leaving overwhelmed families to comb through generic listings, Qrkiez uses AI-driven lead matching to connect the right professional to the right family at the right moment, paired with optimized practice management, all-in-one integration, and practical analytics for providers. This is a novel, defensible model in a sector still dominated by referrals, waitlists, and word of mouth. The commercial model is aligned and frictionless: the first three discovery calls are free, and providers pay a modest per-call fee only when a call is successfully completed. No subscriptions, no risk, revenue that scales directly with value delivered.

The platform is live today on iOS, Android, and web.

The Opportunity

This is a rare opportunity for a leader from within the neurodivergent and therapy sector to define a category. Qrkiez has moved past the hardest part, validating that families want this and providers will pay for it, and is now ready for a chief executive who can turn a proven model into the standard way an entire industry connects care to those who need it.

The next phase of Qrkiez is partnership-led. Rather than signing providers one at a time, we are building agreements with organizations that already hold the trust and the volume of neurodivergent families: therapy and ABA networks, provider groups, pediatric and developmental practices, school and district programs, employer benefits programs, health plans, and national advocacy nonprofits. Each partnership brings supply and demand onto the platform at once.

The role is structured as an equity-first founding executive position. The incoming CEO begins under an equity agreement, taking meaningful ownership in the company and sharing directly in the upside they help create, and elevates to a fully paid, market-compensated CEO role upon a successful fundraise that they help lead. The reward is therefore commensurate with the impact: a leader who disrupts this sector will own a significant piece of the outcome, both financially and in shaping the future of neurodivergent care.

About the Role

The CEO will hold significant equity in Qrkiez and serve as the driving force behind its next phase of growth. The ideal candidate is a builder at heart, someone who has personally tried to scale therapy or neurodivergent support with an entrepreneurial spirit and understands, first-hand, both the promise and the friction of this industry.

We are not going to hand you a plan. We want to hear yours.

Who Thrives in this Role
A background as a therapy provider, psychiatrist, clinical psychologist, or similar practitioner in the neurodivergent or behavioral health space, or deep operating experience in autism and ADHD services, developmental pediatrics, or special education. You know how the money moves in this sector, including regional center funding, insurance and self-determination budgets, school district contracts, and private pay.
A proven entrepreneurial track record: someone who has attempted to scale care delivery or a service network in this industry and knows what works and what breaks.
A closed-deal record with organizations, not individuals. You have signed partnership, channel, or enterprise agreements with provider groups, payers, employers, districts, or large nonprofits, and you can walk us through two of them in detail.
A genuine conviction that AI is the lever to scale access to neurodivergent care, and the vision to apply it responsibly.
Established industry connections, relationships with therapy networks, provider groups, clinics, and referral sources that can be activated quickly. Not a follower count. Named people who will take your call.
Access to funding options for this sector, the credibility and network to open doors with investors focused on healthcare, behavioral health, and impact.
Willingness to be the external face of the company and to sell before there is a large team behind you.

In short, Qrkiez is looking for an operator-clinician: someone with the domain authority to be trusted by providers and families, and the entrepreneurial drive and network to scale a company.

Strong Plus

A clinical background or credential such as PhD, MD, BCBA, SLP, OT, or a state license. This buys immediate trust with providers.
Existing relationships with investors in health, care delivery, or impact.
Lived experience as a neurodivergent adult, or as a parent or sibling in a neurodivergent family.
A point of view on where AI genuinely helps in care matching and where it does not.

A prior CEO title and an advanced clinical degree are welcome but not required.

Goals for This Role

Three things define success here, and all three are yours to shape.
Scale a proven product. Take the established product-market fit and scale it by bringing partners and therapy networks onto the platform, driving significant, repeatable revenue.
Lead the team and the roadmap. Work with the CPO, CTO, and Marketing functions to align future product and go-to-market roadmaps with sector trends and the evolving needs of the neurodivergent community.
Lead the next raise. Co-lead the next round of funding discussions alongside the founding team, the milestone that unlocks the fully paid CEO role.

Compensation and Structure

Equity to start. This is an equity-based role from day one, with meaningful ownership in the company. Specific terms are discussed directly with the founding team.
Salary once we raise. On the close of the next financing, which you help lead, this becomes a full-time salaried position at market compensation.
Location. Bay Area preferred given the initial California focus, though we are open to a remote candidate for the right person. Expect travel to partner sites.

Selection Process

Intro call. Shortlisted candidates have an initial introductory call with the founders to explore mutual fit and vision.
Strategy session. In the second round, candidates develop and present their strategy and ideas for scaling Qrkiez. Bring your own view of where to start: the organizations you would go after and how you would open each.
Final offer. Final offer and equity negotiations are conducted with the founding team.

How to Apply

To apply, send a note to contact@qrkiez.com with what you would go after first and why.

Learn more at www.qrkiez.com

Opportunity

The USC Suzanne Dworak-Peck School of Social Work offers an exceptional opportunity to advance one of the nation's leading schools of social work and a recognized leader in improving health and social outcomes for individuals, families, and communities.

About the Company

Qrkiez is a technology platform transforming how families, individuals, and professionals connect within the neurodivergent care space. Its mission is to empower authentic connections between the neurodivergent community and the professionals who champion their success. Roughly one in five children in the United States is neurodivergent, yet a large share of those individuals and their families struggle to find the right care, and many parents of neurodivergent children report feeling isolated and alone. Qrkiez was built to close that gap.

The platform brings together three pillars that the market has historically kept fragmented: a curated directory of vetted service providers across education, coaching, life skills, enrichment, and wellness; online communities where families and neurodivergent individuals share stories and find belonging; and a wealth of trusted resources and content that cut through the noise and misinformation surrounding neurodivergence. Families and individuals, called QuirkyExplorers, join and use Qrkiez for free, while service providers, called QuirkyPros, build detailed profiles, join or start communities, and engage at no upfront cost.

The transformation Qrkiez brings to the industry is its AI-powered matching engine. Rather than leaving overwhelmed families to comb through generic listings, Qrkiez uses AI-driven lead matching to connect the right professional to the right family at the right moment, paired with optimized practice management, all-in-one integration, and practical analytics for providers. This is a novel, defensible model in a sector still dominated by referrals, waitlists, and word of mouth. The commercial model is aligned and frictionless: the first three discovery calls are free, and providers pay a modest per-call fee only when a call is successfully completed. No subscriptions, no risk, revenue that scales directly with value delivered.

The platform is live today on iOS, Android, and web.

The Opportunity

This is a rare opportunity for a leader from within the neurodivergent and therapy sector to define a category. Qrkiez has moved past the hardest part, validating that families want this and providers will pay for it, and is now ready for a chief executive who can turn a proven model into the standard way an entire industry connects care to those who need it.

The next phase of Qrkiez is partnership-led. Rather than signing providers one at a time, we are building agreements with organizations that already hold the trust and the volume of neurodivergent families: therapy and ABA networks, provider groups, pediatric and developmental practices, school and district programs, employer benefits programs, health plans, and national advocacy nonprofits. Each partnership brings supply and demand onto the platform at once.

The role is structured as an equity-first founding executive position. The incoming CEO begins under an equity agreement, taking meaningful ownership in the company and sharing directly in the upside they help create, and elevates to a fully paid, market-compensated CEO role upon a successful fundraise that they help lead. The reward is therefore commensurate with the impact: a leader who disrupts this sector will own a significant piece of the outcome, both financially and in shaping the future of neurodivergent care.

About the Role

The CEO will hold significant equity in Qrkiez and serve as the driving force behind its next phase of growth. The ideal candidate is a builder at heart, someone who has personally tried to scale therapy or neurodivergent support with an entrepreneurial spirit and understands, first-hand, both the promise and the friction of this industry.

We are not going to hand you a plan. We want to hear yours.

Who Thrives in this Role
A background as a therapy provider, psychiatrist, clinical psychologist, or similar practitioner in the neurodivergent or behavioral health space, or deep operating experience in autism and ADHD services, developmental pediatrics, or special education. You know how the money moves in this sector, including regional center funding, insurance and self-determination budgets, school district contracts, and private pay.
A proven entrepreneurial track record: someone who has attempted to scale care delivery or a service network in this industry and knows what works and what breaks.
A closed-deal record with organizations, not individuals. You have signed partnership, channel, or enterprise agreements with provider groups, payers, employers, districts, or large nonprofits, and you can walk us through two of them in detail.
A genuine conviction that AI is the lever to scale access to neurodivergent care, and the vision to apply it responsibly.
Established industry connections, relationships with therapy networks, provider groups, clinics, and referral sources that can be activated quickly. Not a follower count. Named people who will take your call.
Access to funding options for this sector, the credibility and network to open doors with investors focused on healthcare, behavioral health, and impact.
Willingness to be the external face of the company and to sell before there is a large team behind you.

In short, Qrkiez is looking for an operator-clinician: someone with the domain authority to be trusted by providers and families, and the entrepreneurial drive and network to scale a company.

Strong Plus

Goals for This Role

Three things define success here, and all three are yours to shape.
Scale a proven product. Take the established product-market fit and scale it by bringing partners and therapy networks onto the platform, driving significant, repeatable revenue.
Lead the team and the roadmap. Work with the CPO, CTO, and Marketing functions to align future product and go-to-market roadmaps with sector trends and the evolving needs of the neurodivergent community.
Lead the next raise. Co-lead the next round of funding discussions alongside the founding team, the milestone that unlocks the fully paid CEO role.
